mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% signals labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST > 1000) and retail sales (RSAFS > 400000) indicate robust consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production declining below 100 (2017=100) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1000 (thousands of units) indicates strong residential construction activity that signals economic momentum, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1000.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPIAUCSL inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent price pressures that trigger central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth exceeding 0.5% monthly (PAYEMS) and unemployment below 5.0% (UNRATE) signal labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% MoM and UNRATE is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales growth exceeding 0.3% monthly (RSAFS) signals strong consumer spending that drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during expansionary regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS growth exceeds 0.3% MoM.
